title: Anti-Communism Week, 2025
summary:
The proclamation designates November 2–8, 2025 as Anti-Communism Week, honoring victims of communist regimes and reaffirming a national commitment to individual freedom, human dignity, and democratic values. It portrays communism as a destructive ideology that suppresses faith, speech, and opportunity, and it warns against newer labels that, in the view of the proclamation, promote greater state control at the expense of personal liberty.

Those who may benefit include survivors of communist regimes and their families, human rights advocates, educators, and communities with roots in countries that endured political repression. For them, this week offers recognition, space for remembrance, and a prompt to teach historical lessons about authoritarianism and the importance of civic freedoms. It could also resonate with organizations and policymakers focused on promoting human rights and democratic norms.

Others may feel negatively affected by the framing. People who distinguish democratic socialism or social justice movements from authoritarian communism may see the language as conflating different ideas. Advocates for expanded social programs or labor protections might view the message as politicized or as oversimplifying complex policy debates. There may also be diplomatic sensitivities for countries with communist governments and concerns at home that the tone could deepen polarization rather than invite broad reflection.

In short, the proclamation sets a clear, values-based stance against communism while inviting remembrance of its victims. Its strongest impact is likely among groups focused on human rights and anti-authoritarianism, while its broad language may alienate those who see important differences among political philosophies and policy approaches.
